name: Discrete Mathematics
description: Logic, sets and relations, algebraic structures, counting, recurrences and graph theory for GATE.

nodes.name: Propositional logic
nodes.desc: Connectives, truth tables, implication and its variants; tautologies, contradictions and satisfiability.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build truth tables for compound propositions and classify formulas as tautologies, contradictions or satisfiable.

nodes.name: Equivalence & forms
nodes.desc: Logical equivalence laws, De Morgan, CNF and DNF, and checking whether two formulas say the same thing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prove formulas equivalent with logical laws, convert them to CNF and DNF and test whether two formulas match.

nodes.name: Inference & validity
nodes.desc: Valid arguments, modus ponens and friends, resolution, and logical consequence.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test argument validity using rules of inference, resolution and logical consequence.

nodes.name: Predicate logic
nodes.desc: Predicates, universal and existential quantifiers, nested quantifiers, negation and translating English to first-order logic.
nodes.summary: You will be able to translate English statements into first-order logic with quantifiers and negate quantified statements correctly.

nodes.name: Proof techniques
nodes.desc: Direct proof, contradiction, contrapositive and mathematical induction.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write direct proofs, proofs by contradiction and contrapositive, and proofs by mathematical induction.

nodes.name: Sets & relations
nodes.desc: Set operations and identities, power sets, Cartesian products, relations and their reflexive, symmetric and transitive properties.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply set operations and identities and test relations for reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric and transitive properties.

nodes.name: Equivalence relations
nodes.desc: Equivalence classes, partitions, closures, and counting relations with given properties.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find equivalence classes and partitions, compute closures and count relations with given properties.

nodes.name: Functions
nodes.desc: Injective, surjective and bijective functions, composition, inverses, images and preimages.
nodes.summary: You will be able to classify functions as injective, surjective or bijective and work with composition, inverses, images and preimages.

nodes.name: Countability
nodes.desc: Finite, countable and uncountable sets, cardinality, and diagonalisation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to classify sets as finite, countable or uncountable and prove uncountability by diagonalisation.
topics: Uncountability of reals and power sets

nodes.name: Posets & lattices
nodes.desc: Partial orders, Hasse diagrams, chains and antichains, lub and glb, lattices, distributive and complemented lattices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to draw Hasse diagrams, find bounds in posets and decide whether a lattice is distributive or complemented.
topics: Least upper and greatest lower bounds
Lattices as posets with meet and join

nodes.name: Boolean algebra
nodes.desc: Boolean algebra as a complemented distributive lattice; the link between posets and logic circuits.
nodes.summary: You will be able to recognise Boolean algebras as complemented distributive lattices and connect them to logic circuits.

nodes.name: Groups
nodes.desc: Binary operations, closure, associativity, identity and inverses; groups and abelian groups, often over modular arithmetic.
nodes.summary: You will be able to check group axioms for an operation, often modular arithmetic, and identify abelian groups.

nodes.name: Semigroups & monoids
nodes.desc: The algebraic ladder: groupoid, semigroup, monoid, group; checking each axiom on a given operation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to classify an algebraic structure as a groupoid, semigroup, monoid or group by checking each axiom.

nodes.name: Subgroups & Lagrange
nodes.desc: Subgroups, cosets, Lagrange's theorem, cyclic groups and generators, element orders.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find subgroups and cosets, apply Lagrange's theorem and work with cyclic groups, generators and element orders.

nodes.name: Counting principles
nodes.desc: Sum and product rules, permutations, counting strings and subsets.
nodes.summary: You will be able to count arrangements using the sum and product rules, permutations and counts of strings and subsets.

nodes.name: Combinations
nodes.desc: Binomial coefficients, multisets and stars and bars, distributions of identical and distinct objects, lattice paths.
nodes.summary: You will be able to count selections and distributions with binomial coefficients, multisets, stars and bars and lattice paths.

nodes.name: Inclusion–exclusion
nodes.desc: Inclusion–exclusion, counting onto functions and derangements, and the pigeonhole principle.
nodes.summary: You will be able to count with inclusion-exclusion, including onto functions and derangements, and apply the pigeonhole principle.

nodes.name: Catalan & identities
nodes.desc: Catalan numbers, the ballot problem, double counting and summation identities.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply Catalan numbers and the ballot problem and prove identities by double counting.

nodes.name: Recurrence relations
nodes.desc: Setting up recurrences for counting problems; solving linear homogeneous and non-homogeneous recurrences via the characteristic equation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to set up recurrences for counting problems and solve linear recurrences with the characteristic equation.

nodes.name: Generating functions
nodes.desc: Ordinary generating functions for sequences and counting, and solving recurrences with them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use ordinary generating functions to represent sequences, count combinations and solve recurrences.

nodes.name: Graph basics
nodes.desc: Graph types, degree and the handshaking lemma, complete and bipartite graphs, adjacency representations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe graph types, apply the handshaking lemma and represent graphs with adjacency matrices and lists.

nodes.name: Paths & connectivity
nodes.desc: Walks, paths and cycles, connected components, cut vertices and edges, diameter, Euler and Hamiltonian paths.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse walks, paths, cycles and connectivity and decide whether Euler or Hamiltonian paths exist.

nodes.name: Trees & spanning trees
nodes.desc: Properties of trees and forests, counting spanning trees and Cayley's formula.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prove properties of trees and forests and count spanning trees, including with Cayley's formula.

nodes.name: Planar graphs
nodes.desc: Euler's formula, face counting, K5 and K3,3, and Kuratowski's theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply Euler's formula to planar graphs, count faces and test planarity with Kuratowski's theorem.

nodes.name: Colouring & covers
nodes.desc: Chromatic number, independent sets, vertex covers, cliques and matchings.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find chromatic numbers and relate independent sets, vertex covers, cliques and matchings.

nodes.name: Isomorphism
nodes.desc: Graph isomorphism and invariants, complements and self-complementary graphs, counting graphs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test graphs for isomorphism using invariants, work with complements and count labelled graphs.
